# A stochastic bulk receiver for finite affine trapping families

Author-derived work, 2026-11-02. No independent whole audit, historical novelty claim, or complete positive-recurrence theorem is asserted. This is intended as a substantial intermediate operation toward the arbitrary-dimensional recurrence problem, rather than a new recognized chemical architecture.

## Statement being developed

Let a finite weakly reversible mass-action network have positive rates, integer complexes, finite maximal source degree D, and stoichiometric space S. Fix a positive affine compatibility class P=(c+S) intersected with the positive orthant. Suppose P contains a point c with c_i>=1; otherwise the eventual logarithmic bulk considered below is empty. The claim is that the finite affine-family construction described below yields a nonnegative normlike function V on the whole count orthant and finite constants C,N0 such that

    L V(x) <= -1

for every count state x in c+S with N=max_i x_i>=N0 and min_i x_i>=C log(2+N).

The generator is the ACTUAL falling-factorial generator. No stationarity, spectral gap, fast equilibration, normalized frozen fiber, volume limit, or mixing-time hypothesis is used. V is not claimed to dissipate on the complementary low-count faces. Those faces include the catalytic bottleneck and are the remaining central obstacle; this statement alone does not prove recurrence.

The argument uses the finite affine approximation lemma from OpenAI, *Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems*, October 5, 2026, sections affine.tex and trapping.tex. That source proves a deterministic theorem and does not itself provide the stochastic receiver here. Its repository identifies the collection as research data of mixed verification status. The source lemma is a governing mathematical input, not an independently audited Astra theorem or an uncharged software oracle.

## 1. Exact smooth-minimum jump estimate

Let L_i(x)=r_i.x+b_i, i in a finite set I, theta>0, and

    Ftheta(x)=-theta log(sum_i exp(-L_i(x)/theta)).
    p_i(x)=exp(-L_i(x)/theta)/sum_j exp(-L_j(x)/theta).

Let the finitely many actual jumps be nu_e, with rates q_e(x)>=0, and set

    R=max_(i,e) |r_i.nu_e|,
    Gamma_i(x)=sum_e q_e(x)|r_i.nu_e|,
    d_i(x)=sum_e q_e(x) r_i.nu_e,
    delta=R exp(R/theta)/(2 theta).

The exact, finite-jump inequality is

    L(-Ftheta)(x) <= sum_i p_

# Fixed-width bulk upgrade

Author-derived and unaudited. This strengthens the weaker logarithmic-bulk construction in `BULK_CONSTRUCTION.md`; that file is preserved as the initial derivation. The global function, exact finite-jump bound, source-cut proof, classwise plateau exclusion, normalization and scale gluing remain the same. The improvement is a sharper use of the acquired active-region distance.

## Theorem

Subject to the governing finite affine-family lemma cited and read in the preceding construction, every finite weakly reversible mass-action network with fixed positive rates admits, on each positive affine compatibility class, a nonnegative normlike function V on the count orthant with

    L V(x)<=-1

outside a class-dependent finite set wherever EVERY coordinate is at least K=max(1,2D), where D is the largest source degree. The assertion covers arbitrary dimension and arbitrary linkage multiplicity. It is a BULK statement, not general recurrence: the union of excluded strips x_i<K is infinite. No bound uniform across conserved enzyme pools or actual communication classes is silently supplied.

If the compatibility class has no point with all coordinates >=1, its bulk is empty. Otherwise choose a single such c as the representative in the affine construction. A count state in the bulk has all sources enabled, and actual falling factorials are uniformly comparable to monomials. No high-volume or continuum limit occurs.

## The strengthened near-active calculation

Write n=min x_i, N=max x_i, R>=2N, and retain affine labels active somewhere in [1,R]^d as before. Their slopes are nonpositive, and the uniform Hoffman constant B is acquired from fixed coefficient matrices. Let

    ell=L log(2+N),

where L is a finite constant chosen below. Call a label near-active when its affine gap is at most ell. It has an actual active point z in [1,R]^d with

    |z-x|_infinity<=B ell.

Both x and z have every coordinate at least one. Hence, even when some x_i are bounded, every coordinate ratio between them is between

    1/(1+B ell) and 1+B ell.

The original derivation unnecessarily demanded a factor-two ratio, which required n to grow logarithmically. A polylogarithmic distortion is enough. If r_i.u<r_i.v, the primary source sign-gap lemma at z gives

    z^v/z^u<=R^(-H),
    x^v/x^u<=(1+B ell)^(|v-u|_1) R^(-H)
              <=(1+B ell)^(2D) R^(-H).

Finite checks of an exact finite-jump inequality, kink failure of a naive rule, and actual source-cut arithmetic.
